items.title: Introduction to Consciousness
items.question: What does it mean to be conscious?
items.description: A first course on what the word consciousness covers, why subjective experience is hard to study, and how scientists and philosophers approach it. It treats open questions as open.
items.audience: Curious readers with no background in neuroscience or philosophy.
objectives: Explain several important meanings of consciousness.
Distinguish subjective experience from related cognitive functions.
Identify significant approaches to studying consciousness.
Explain why consciousness remains an active area of scientific and philosophical investigation.
items.durationBasis: Estimated from word count (about 180 words a minute) plus 4 minutes for the activity and 1 minute per knowledge check.

items.title: Foundations of Artificial Intelligence
items.question: How do artificial intelligence systems learn, reason, and generate responses?
items.description: A first course on what AI is, how machine learning and neural networks work, how language models generate text, and how AI systems are evaluated. It does not treat all AI systems as the same kind of machine.
items.audience: Readers with no technical background. Three lessons include small working demonstrations.
objectives: Explain what the term artificial intelligence covers and what it leaves out.
Describe how a machine learning system learns from examples.
Explain at a basic level how neural networks and language models work.
Describe how AI capabilities are evaluated and why evaluation is hard.
Distinguish intelligence-like behaviour from consciousness, and name limitations and risks.
items.durationBasis: Estimated from word count (about 180 words a minute) plus 4 minutes for the activity and 1 minute per knowledge check.
